a man should accomplish his affairs with that and not with others except in times of distress.

Śrīdhara: He states the duties of the stages of life (āśrama-dharma) concisely with the words "That which... and so forth. "That" refers to the object; "by which" refers to the means; "from whom" refers to the source. ||66||
*Krama-sandarbha*: Not commented upon.
*Viśvanātha*: He states the duties of the stages of life (*āśrama-dharma*) concisely: "Whatever substance," "by whatever means," and "from whichever source. (66)
O King, a man who abides by these and other duties prescribed in the Vedas, while remaining at home, shall attain the same goal as him if he possesses devotion to Him.
Śrīdhara concludes the subject at hand with the words "by these": "his path" refers to that of this Śrī Kṛṣṇa;
"one who possesses devotion to him" means his devotee. ||67||
*Krama-sandarbha*: Not commented upon.

*Viśvanātha*: He concludes the subject at hand with the words "by these" (*etair*). The meaning is: even a householder, while remaining in his home, may partake in the devotion to this Śrī Kṛṣṇa if he follows His path. (67)
Just as you, O King and God, have delivered yourself from this multitude of calamities so difficult to escape, O Lord;
By serving the lotus-feet of whom you,
having conquered the elephants of the quarters, performed sacrifices.

Śrīdhara: This has been stated as being common to all; however, for the devotee, devotion alone is the cause of all human goals (*puruṣārtha*). With this in mind, he speaks specifically regarding the Pāṇḍavas, beginning with "yathā hi" (just as). O King of kings! [It was obtained] from one who is difficult to abandon even by kings and gods acting as allies, or from the Self.
"From Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa alone"—the absence of the augment *ṭi* (in *prabhoh*) is an archaic Vedic usage; the meaning is "having arrived here with excellence.

The ellipsis is "worship Him alone, exactly as He is. Or else: just as you have emerged from the multitude of calamities, and just as you performed the sacrifices, so too [emerge] from the ocean of worldly existence through the Savior, Śrī Kṛṣṇa alone.
The meaning is "from the north. ||68||

The sequence of the composition: Just as by that very mode of devotion alone, for the sake of your own Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa, you have crossed over and shall continue to cross over the multitude of calamities; he confirms that very point with the words "yat" (that). ||68||
Viśvanātha: This work of five chapters has been spoken for the sake of all people in general;

however, for those who are exclusively devoted—whether they are perfected souls (*siddhas*) or spiritual practitioners (*sādhakas*)—the Lord alone is their goal. And therein, the Lord, having himself become directly manifest to the perfected ones, dances them upon the waves of his own love.

He causes them to undergo prosperity, adversity, and the cycles of fortune exactly as they should; they likewise perform that which he intends, for their service consists solely in acting according to his will. Regarding this, taking the Pāṇḍavas themselves as the authoritative example, he says: "For just as... [they were freed] from calamities difficult to escape, even with kings and gods as allies.
From his own master, [he attained excellence] through service at his feet characterized by meditation and other such practices; that is to say, he excelled.

Just as you, sir, performed sacrifices by means of that very service, so too do others such as Ugrasena and the rest serve him—this is the implied meaning. Therefore, one like me is a fool whose intellect is deluded by domestic life.
The meaning is that, having said this, it should not be thought that their inclusion within the duties of householders is impossible. ||68||
— I was formerly a certain Gandharva named Upabarhaṇa,
highly esteemed among the Gandharvas in a past great aeon.
Regarding *madhvaḥ*: it is stated that in the past *mahā-kalpa*, the past *brahma-kalpa*, the time of Brahmā (*brahma-kāla*), the supreme (*para*), and the *mahā-kalpa* are all synonymous. (69)
Śrīdhara: Showing that service to Śrī Kṛṣṇa is lost through the contempt of the great and is accomplished through their grace, he relates a past event with five and a half verses beginning with "I...
[The sage was] Upabarhaṇa by name. (69)
The sequence of composition: therein, he provides an illustration of his own case with the words beginning "I," etc.; among those, the pair beginning with "I" [is explained] in verse 69.

Viśvanātha: Regarding those practitioners who have attained devotion through spontaneous association with the saintly, the Blessed Lord Himself instructs them in the form of the Śrīmad Bhāgavata scripture, as in the verse beginning, "But he who, having abandoned all duties, worships Me alone—he is the most excellent" (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 11.11.32); and they act exactly according to His direction.

They act thus, taking as their sole authority the scriptural injunction spoken by the Blessed One: "Having abandoned the stages of life (āśramas) along with their emblems, one should wander beyond the scope of prescribed rules" (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 11.18.28).
Consequently, they do not regard the conduct and duties of the social classes and stages of life (varṇāśrama-dharma), considering their own previous birth alone as the relevant factor.
Establishing this as the authority, he says with five and a half verses beginning with "I": ||69||
He is beautiful in form, sweet, fragrant, and pleasing to behold;
he is eternally beloved by women, intoxicated, and addicted to his own city.
Śrīdhara: He whose appearance is charming, delicate, and pleasing due to his beauty and other qualities. ||70||
Kramasandarbha: Not explained. Viśvanātha: "Peśalam" means cleverness. ||70||
Once, at a divine sacrifice, the hosts of Gandharvas and Apsarases were invited by the creators of the universe to sing songs in praise of Hari.
It has not been explained by anyone at all.
And I, knowing that, went forth surrounded by women while singing.
Having learned of my offense against the Creator of the universe, they cursed me with their power:
"Go quickly to the state of a Śūdra, your fortune destroyed, for you have committed an act of contempt."
Śrīdhara and Viśvanātha: Knowing that to be his summons, the wise man went away while singing like one intoxicated. ||72||
The sequence of the composition has not been explained.
—o)0(o— First, I was born as a maidservant; even there, I was among those who discourse upon Brahman.
Through the constant practice of service, I have attained the status of a son of Brahmā.
Śrīdhara: Not commented upon.
Viśvanātha: "Even there" means even in the case of birth as a Śūdra; or, when such a curse has occurred.
Here, the narration of such a historical account is for the purpose of making known the prior state of devotion, as a secondary consequence.
Again and again, through attachment or through favorable attachment. ||73||
You have described those household duties that destroy evil,
by which a householder may easily attain the path of the renunciants.
Śrīdhara and Viśvanātha have not commented [on this].
Krama-sandarbha: The meaning of the section is that by that very same mode of devotion alone, I attained even the status of Nārada. ||74||
O,
you are indeed highly fortunate in the world of men; as sages, you approach purifying the world.
He in whose house [the Lord] dwells is the Supreme Brahman itself, manifest yet hidden, appearing in human form.

In this regard, the collection of Sāṅkhya verses found in Bhāgavatam 7.10.48–50 should be consulted again, verse by verse. It should be understood that this repetition is indeed due to [the author's] great respect.
Śrīdhara: "But you have indeed achieved your purpose"—with this joy, he recites those very previous verses again, beginning with "You all. The rest is clear. ||75||
*Krama-sandarbha*: Not explained.

*Viśvanātha*: But you are as preeminent among all devotees such as Prahlāda as you are the most supreme among the social classes beginning with the Brahmins and among the stages of life beginning with studentship (*brahmacarya*).
Elucidating the very same three verses mentioned previously, he speaks again: "You... (verse 75).
This indeed is that Brahman, the experience of the bliss of Nirvana, the absolute liberation sought by the great.
He is indeed your beloved friend, your maternal cousin, worthy of honoring as himself, the ordainer of rites, and your preceptor.
It has not been explained by anyone at all—
not even directly by Bhava, Padmaja, and the others.
May this Lord of the Sātvatas, who has been described as a reality through the intellect and worshipped with silence, devotion, and tranquility, be pleased.

Śrīdhara: "Oh, the good fortune of Prahlāda, by whom the Lord was seen! We, however, are unfortunate. To the king who was thus despondent, [the sage] replied with three verses beginning with "You... [stating]: "The Supreme Brahman does not dwell in the house of Prahlāda, nor do sages [reside there] for the sake of seeing Him."

Therefore, they go to his home; yet his *brahma* (spiritual power) does not reside in the form of his maternal cousins and so forth, nor is it manifest within himself alone. Thus, the sense is: "You yourselves are far more fortunate than even he, and indeed more so than we. (77)
The sequence of composition by Viśvanātha has not been explained. —
